title: st edit writes on its rc=1 refusal for a known thread, and the remedy names an empty list
body:
`intent st edit <KNOWN-ID> <authored-file>` still registers the thread in the TRACKED `intent/.intentfiles` and then fails, when that file is not realised. This is the half of 0144 that 0144 did not close, and it is the commoner case: 0144's subject was a typo'd id, this one fires on a thread you actually have.

MEASURED ON THE `30a2dd81` PAIR, on a throwaway project (`intent init` + `intent st new`), manifest present with content, `.intentfiles` restored from a pristine copy before the arm, and the instrument positive-controlled first (a known-good write moved the hash):

    st edit ST0001 design   -> rc=1, .intentfiles grows 1652 -> 1671 bytes

The write survives the refusal, so a realisation-policy diff nobody made is left in the working tree for whoever commits next. In a five-node shared checkout that is somebody else's commit.

AND THE REFUSAL'S REMEDY IS VACUOUS ON THIS PATH, which is a second defect on the same line and is why this is filed as one issue rather than two:

    error: `intent/st/ST0001/design.md` is not a file this artefact carries
    remedy: this artefact carries: 

Nothing after the colon. The remedy exists to name the alternatives and names none, so the operator is told what they cannot do and not what they can. This belongs with the vacuous-`doctor`-remedy item on hv's parked stack as ONE class, not as two sightings.

PROVENANCE. cc predicted this case from reading the code while fixing 0144 -- an unknown id now returns `NoSuchThread` and never reaches `NoSuchEditable`, but a KNOWN thread carrying no realised file still reaches it with an empty `present` list -- and stated plainly that they had not measured it. vc measured it as a control arm while verifying the 0144 fix. The hypothesis is cc's; the measurement is vc's.

NOT A REGRESSION FROM 0144. Driven against the same binary in the same run: the unknown-id arms (`hydrate`, and `edit` with design/impl/tasks/info) all return rc=1, write nothing, and print one uniform message. 0144 is correctly closed; its scope was simply narrower than the class.
